call_points.text: No numeric revenue, margin or order inflow guidance is given for FY27.
Consolidated core EBITDA margin fell to 9.8% from 12.2% a year ago.
Consolidated finance cost rose 42.2% YoY to ₹107.0 Cr in Q1FY27.
MoR decided in principle to close IRSDC, with station development work moving to RLDA.
FY27 revenue guided at similar levels to FY26, about ₹9,000 Cr, down from the ₹10,000-11,000 Cr guided earlier.
call_points.versus_prior: lowered from ₹10,000-11,000 Cr guided at the Q2 call

call_points.text: Standalone core EBITDA margin guided at 4.0-4.2% for FY27 as competitive bids go below estimates.
Order book of about ₹25,000 Cr, with projects running two and a half to three years.
JV profit share guided at ₹70-80 Cr going forward, with CERL losses expected to break even in two years.
Gulf crisis and energy prices are a risk; NHAI has issued a clarification compensating abnormal bitumen price increases.
No official communication from the government on any Ircon-RVNL merger.
About 53.9% of the order book was won on competitive bidding, the rest on nomination.

operating_notes.text: Order book ₹24,984 Cr at 31.03.2026: 54% railways, 46% highways; 78% domestic, 22% international; 53.9% won on competitive bidding.
FY26 consolidated other income of ₹430.9 Cr was 34% of EBITDA; core EBITDA (excluding other income) was ₹848.4 Cr.
Standalone core EBITDA margin was 4.2% in FY26 versus 4.7% in FY25, while consolidated core margin was 9.4%.
Order book stood at ₹24,984 crore as of March 31, 2026.
FY26 bid success rate on value was about 10%, up from 6% in FY24-25 and 5.7% in FY23-24.
Order book at 31 March 2026 was 92% domestic and 8% international, with 54% won on competitive bidding and 46% on nomination.
Own cash was about ₹950 Cr of the ~₹4,200 Cr reported, the rest being project-specific funds and client advances.
Order book of ₹23,366 Cr at 30 June 2026 is split 77% Railways, 16% Highways and 7% Others, and 91% domestic.
About 55% of the order book was won on competitive bidding and 45% on nomination.
Consolidated finance cost rose to ₹107.0 Cr in Q1FY27 from ₹75.2 Cr a year ago, with FY26 at ₹350.1 Cr.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,188.98 Cr (-6.5% YoY), net profit ₹191.46 Cr (-9.6% YoY).
Ircon's Q4 & FY26 investor presentation (22 May 2026) showed consolidated revenue down 15.7% to ₹9,071 Cr and PAT down 18.7% to ₹591.9 Cr, with an order book of ₹24,984 Cr at 31 March 2026.
On May 22, 2026, Ircon reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹3,189.0 Cr and recommended a final dividend of Re 0.70 per share.
IRCON International Limited shared the audio recording link of its conference call on May 25, 2026, discussing Q4FY26 and FY2026 results.
On 25 May 2026 Ircon's Q4 & FY26 analyst call guided FY27 revenue flat at about ₹9,000 Cr, down from ₹10,000-11,000 Cr earlier, with standalone core EBITDA margin at 4.0-4.2%.
On May 27, 2026, Ircon received ₹9.56 lakh fines each from NSE and BSE for board composition non-compliance.
In October 2026, Ircon International announced that the NSE favorably considered its application for the waiver of compliance fines.
